newsitem.title: USA: New England college applications flat this year.
newsitem.headline: New England college applications flat this year.

text.p: The number of students applying to colleges in the Northeast region turned flat after two years of single-digit increases, according to a survey released Tuesday.

That may reflect a decline in the number of applications per college student rather than the number of graduating high school seniors, said Wendy Lindsay, associate director of the New England Board of Higher Education.
"One of our guesses is that there are probably fewer multiple applications. The actual number of students applying has not dropped," she told Reuters.

The NEBHE found in a survey of the more than 200 colleges in the six-state region that only 53 percent of the schools reported an increase for fall 1997 freshman applications, compared with 74 percent last year.
Applications to schools rose four percent and five percent respectively during the previous two years, the survey found.
Many of the schools have rolling application deadlines, and at least 168 colleges in the region are still taking applications as of May 1, the survey found.

A further 14 schools were closed to freshmen but would consider transfer applications and only 36 of the region's undergraduate institutions were not taking additional freshmen or transfer applications, the survey found.
The costs of multiple applications and the growing popularity of early enrollment programs was likely keeping the number of applications down, Lindsay said.
Students are also becoming more active in shopping for the best financial aid package, she said.

"People are taking a hard look at what it costs to go to college and lobbying to get the best financial aide package," she said. "One officer said they are almost looking at it like they would a home purchase, trying to get the best package."
